airport.name: Elizabeth City Regional Airport & Coast Guard Air Station

summary: Elizabeth City Regional Airport & Coast Guard Air Station (ECG/KECG) is a dual-use public airport located in northeastern North Carolina, sharing its facilities with U.S. Coast Guard Air Station Elizabeth City, one of the largest Coast Guard aviation facilities on the East Coast. Originally established as a Naval Air Station during World War II, it continues to serve both civilian general aviation and active Coast Guard operations, including search and rescue missions along the mid-Atlantic coast.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Elizabeth City Regional Airport?
A: The airport primarily serves general aviation and charter flights, as it does not currently have scheduled commercial airline service.

Q: Why is the Coast Guard Air Station located here?
A: Its strategic position near the Outer Banks and Albemarle Sound makes it ideal for Coast Guard search and rescue, law enforcement, and maritime patrol operations along the mid-Atlantic coast.

Q: Can civilians access the Coast Guard facilities?
A: Access to the Coast Guard side is restricted, but the civilian terminal and general aviation areas are open to the public during regular hours.

Q: Is there an FBO at ECG?
A: Yes, the airport has fixed-base operator services that provide fuel, hangar space, and ground handling for general aviation aircraft.
transport_tips: The airport is located about 7 miles southeast of downtown Elizabeth City and is easily reached via US Highway 17. Rental cars and taxi services are available, though advance arrangements are recommended since on-site rental counters may have limited hours. Ample free parking is available close to the terminal for both short and extended visits.
local_tip: If you're visiting, take a short drive to the nearby waterfront downtown Elizabeth City, where you can watch large Coast Guard and Navy vessels transit through the Dismal Swamp Canal route, and grab fresh seafood at one of the locally owned restaurants on Water Street.
